business_scope.primary_industry_name: Mail-Order Retail with Cash on Delivery Settlement

stage_1.executive_summary: Stage 1 pre-incorporation due diligence for a contemplated Canadian Unlimited Liability Corporation (ULC) registered in Alberta (CA-AB), engaged in ISIC 4791 / NAICS 454110 mail-order retail with cash-on-delivery settlement targeting emerging markets. Key findings: (i) Alberta does not authorize ULC incorporation under the Business Corporations Act (RSA 2000, c B-9); a true ULC must be domiciled in British Columbia or Nova Scotia and extra-provincially registered in Alberta; (ii) Canada is not a Contracting State to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, so all Canadian-issued documents require consular legalization through Global Affairs Canada and the destination consulate; (iii) UBO disclosure to the Canadian beneficial-ownership registers is government-access-only, with a 25% reporting threshold; (iv) the COD model is classified Medium_Risk_Enhanced, requiring strict quarantine of cash remittance to licensed money-service businesses such as Airwallex; (v) estimated Stage 1 budget is approximately USD 3,040 inclusive of fallback incorporation fees.

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid Federal-Provincial System: Canadian federalism; Alberta is a common law province; corporate law is provincial under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, while AML/CFT and criminal law are federal under the PCMLTFA and the Criminal Code
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: USMCA (Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement), entered into force 2020
CPTPP (Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership), entered into force 2018
CETA (Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement), provisionally applied 2017
Canada-China Agreement on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments, entered into force 2014
Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement, entered into force 2015
Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980), as amended by the Fifth Protocol (2007)
meta_jurisdiction_context.entity_structure_caveat: Alberta does not provide for Unlimited Liability Corporation formation under the ABCA. Authentic ULC status is available only in British Columbia (Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57, s 51.1) and Nova Scotia (Companies Act, RSNS 1989, c 81). The compliant pathway for the requested composite key (CA_AB + CA_ULC) is: (a) incorporate a BC or NS ULC, and (b) register it as an extra-provincial corporation in Alberta under the ABCA. If an Alberta-domiciled entity is mandatory, the close substitutes are a standard ABCA corporation or an Alberta unlimited-liability-style limited liability partnership, with corresponding U.S. federal tax classification analysis.
meta_jurisdiction_context.cross_border_tax_note: Under the Canada-US Tax Convention (1980, as amended by the Fifth Protocol 2007), a ULC is a resident Canadian corporation for treaty purposes. U.S. shareholders may elect to treat the ULC as a disregarded entity under U.S. check-the-box rules (Treas. Reg. s 301.7701-3), generating U.S. Form 8858 flow-through reporting; however, the ULC remains subject to Canadian Part I income tax and Part XIII withholding on distributions to non-residents. A written cross-border tax opinion is required prior to capitalization, and prior to any election to be treated as an unlimited liability company for U.S. tax purposes.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA); Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, s 462.31; Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c 1 (5th Supp); Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss 21.1-21.5 (individuals with significant control), as amended by the Budget Implementation Act, 2023, with public beneficial-ownership filing obligations effective January 22, 2024. Provincial: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9; if BC-domiciled: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57, including BC beneficial-ownership transparency legislation applicable to the proposed ULC; extra-provincial registration rules under ABCA Part 21.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, British Columbia; or Registrar of Joint Stock Companies, Nova Scotia; or Registrar of Corporations, Alberta (Service Alberta)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization: Global Affairs Canada (Authentication Services Section) attestation followed by legalization at the consular post of the destination jurisdiction; Canada is not a Contracting State to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Status / Certificate of Good Standing (current, dated)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) or BC Corporate Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization: Global Affairs Canada + consular post of destination jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: NUANS corporate name search report (name clearance evidence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: NUANS operator / authorized Corporate Registry service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization: Global Affairs Canada + consular post of destination jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified extract of the register of individuals with significant control (ISC/UBO register)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The ULC itself, board-certified and notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization then Consular Legalization: Global Affairs Canada + consular post of destination jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passport and proof of residential address for each director, officer, and 25%+ beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin / competent issuing authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization route in source country, then attestation at Canadian consular post if the document is to be used in Canada; or Global Affairs Canada + destination consulate if issued in Canada

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against: (i) Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; (ii) the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky), SC 2017, c 21; (iii) the United Nations Act, SC 1991, c 45 and UN Security Council sanctions lists; (iv) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) list; (v) UK HMT consolidated sanctions list; (vi) EU consolidated sanctions list; and (vii) Interpol notices. PEP status must be screened through commercial databases (World-Check One, Dow Jones, Refinitiv) and documented in the AML/CFT compliance program. Enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, and cash-intensive emerging-market corridors. FINTRAC suspicious transaction reports (STRs) are mandatory as soon as reasonable grounds exist under PCMLTFA s 7.1; large cash and virtual currency transaction reporting thresholds apply at CAD 10,000.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.payment_rails_aml_commentary: The COD settlement model involves third-party logistics agents collecting cash and remitting through licensed money-service businesses. The ULC must not itself handle cash remittance or foreign exchange, or it will become a FINTRAC-reporting Money Services Business under the PCMLTFA. Contracting with Airwallex (Airwallex (Canada) Inc., FINTRAC-registered MSB) and local licensed remitters is AML-compliant only where the ULC executes written AML/KYC protocols with each logistics/collection agent, maintains source-of-funds documentation for high-risk corridors, and ensures suspicious-transaction escalation to FINTRAC. The ULC should further require contractual indemnities from logistics partners for any unlicensed money transmission.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry at https://www.albertacorporateregistry.ca (filings through authorized service providers with a NUANS name search report); alternative BC domicile: British Columbia Corporate Online at https://www.corporateonline.gov.bc.ca.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in Roman script (English and/or French only). Chinese characters or other non-Roman scripts are not accepted in the Canadian corporate register; any foreign-language name must be transliterated into a Romanized form and pass the NUANS search. The legal element must reflect the entity type: 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Company' for a BC/NS ULC, and 'Limited', 'Ltee', 'Incorporated', 'Inc.', 'Corporation', 'Corp.', or 'Ltd.' for an ABCA corporation. An Alberta extra-provincial registration must use the exact corporate name of the home jurisdiction as cleared through Alberta NUANS.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Alberta Corporate Registry rejects a name (NUANS conflict, prohibited token, or deception), the applicant must obtain a fresh NUANS report and resubmit a revised incorporation or extra-provincial registration. There is no statutory administrative appeal for requested name approval; the practical remedies are: (i) written reconsideration request to Service Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of refusal; (ii) filing under a corrected/distinguishable name within the remaining validity window; or (iii) judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSA 2000, c J-3, where the refusal was arbitrary or ultra vires. A rejected name is not protected and may be taken by another applicant.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.jurisdictional_variation_note: For a BC-domiciled ULC registering extra-provincially in Alberta, the BC name approval/report validity is 56 days whereas the Alberta NUANS report is valid for 90 days. Both windows must be coordinated; name clearance in BC does not guarantee clearance in Alberta because each register applies its own distinguishability test.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for the statutory registered office only if a physical street address in Alberta is maintained (no P.O. Box), service of process can be accepted during ordinary business hours, and the provider is a licensed corporate registered-office agent. Virtual office arrangements are routinely accepted by the Alberta Corporate Registry and are suitable for a mail-order e-commerce retailer with no physical storefront. However, CRA and financial institutions (Airwallex KYC) will expect evidence of actual management substance; a bare virtual office with non-resident directors increases CRA audit risk and may affect GST/HST non-resident registration obligations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspection: Alberta Corporate Registry compliance visit below 2% per year absent third-party complaint; CRA GST/HST or income tax audit/verification for a new cross-border e-commerce entity approximately 10-15% within the first 3 years; FINTRAC examination below 5% per year provided the ULC remains a non-reporting retailer and outsources all money transmission and FX to licensed MSBs (Airwallex and local licensed remitters).
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.commercial_substance_note: The ULC should maintain Canadian-resident decision-making records, board minutes, bank accounts, and contractual records in Alberta/Canada. A non-resident-owned ULC with no substantive Canadian commercial substance may be challenged by CRA on residency and treaty-benefit access, and may be treated as a Canadian-resident taxpayer under common law residential-ties analysis.

stage_1.legal_disclaimer: This dossier is a pre-incorporation due diligence analysis and does not constitute a legal opinion. Actual fees are subject to regulator tariff revisions, exchange-rate fluctuation, and engagement-specific counsel rates. The ULC structure must be confirmed against the laws of British Columbia or Nova Scotia (incorporation) and Alberta (extra-provincial registration) before any filing. Independent advice from a Canadian corporate and international tax counsel is mandatory prior to incorporation, capitalization, and the execution of COD remittance agreements.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 6-20 (incorporation, articles, registered office) and ss. 101-122 (directors and officers); Business Corporations Regulations, AR 262/2001
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / Registrar of Corporations, Service Alberta, e-filing through the Corporate Registry System (CORES)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1 pursuant to the Business Corporations Regulations, AR 262/2001)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow account for an Alberta ULC. Shareholder contributions are fixed in the Articles of Incorporation or shareholders agreement; liability is unlimited as regards the obligations of the corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED: (1) The Articles of Incorporation filed by the sole incorporator are adopted, and the authorized capital structure consisting of one class of unlimited-liability common shares is confirmed. (2) The subscription by the initial shareholder for 100 common shares at CAD 0.01 per share is accepted, and such shares are issued upon payment. (3) The registered office address in Alberta and the registered office agent named in the Articles are ratified. (4) The President and Secretary are appointed as officers. (5) Banking resolutions and corporate-seal authorities are approved, effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Corporate Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES) via an authorized service provider or NUANS search provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a Government of Canada NUANS search for the proposed corporate name. Ensure the name includes the proper legal element 'Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC'. If desired, file a name reservation before incorporation. Submit the approved NUANS report and any required consent letters together with the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Consent letter if the name contains a third-party distinctive element
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as confusingly similar, resubmit with alternate names through CORES or request reconsideration by Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Articles of Incorporation and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and legal counsel; no Crown filing at this step
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name, registered office address within Alberta, share structure, board composition, and any permitted restrictions. Execute signature pages as incorporator; obtain signed consents to act as directors, registered office consent, and ULC liability acknowledgment. Verify all statutory contents required by the Business Corporations Act (Alberta).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing portal identifies defects before submission, amend and re-execute the Articles and consents; if asked for supplemental evidence, provide corrected documents with updated execution dates.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles of Incorporation and Pay Filing Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry via CORES
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles of Incorporation electronically through CORES, attach the director consents and registered office consent, and pay the required filing fee. Once processed, the Registry will issue the Certificate of Incorporation and an Access Code for maintaining corporate records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, cure the objection by filing amended Articles or corrected consents within the Registry's stated response period and pay any applicable administrative fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Business Number and Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online; Alberta Corporate Tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, use the CRA Business Number creation process with the corporate Access Code to obtain a Business Number. Register for GST/HST if the corporation will make taxable supplies, payroll account if employees will be hired, and review the appropriate Alberta provincial tax registration. Confirm the ULC's tax characterization with a tax advisor.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA cannot match incorporation data, call the CRA Business Window, supply the certificate of incorporation, and resubmit the registration with corrected particulars.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish Statutory Corporate Records and Banking Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office and board of directors of the ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or adopt the written first board resolution adopting the Articles, ratifying share issuance, appointing officers, and approving a corporate banking resolution. Prepare the share certificate for the initial shareholder, open the corporate bank account, update the shareholders register, and record the annual return calendar.
required_dossiers: Corporate minute book and share records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or counterparty rejects the board resolution for lack of signature or proper officer title, provide an incumbency certificate, certified corporate resolution, and corporate register excerpt.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Municipal Business Licence and Physical Occupancy Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality (e.g., City of Calgary or City of Edmonton) and Alberta Fire Safety Codes branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal General Business Licence for the registered operating address. If leasing a warehouse, obtain a development permit / occupancy permit under the Alberta Building Code, and arrange a fire safety inspection under the Alberta Fire Code before operations begin. Confirm the physical premises is zoned for mail-order retail and logistics.
required_dossiers: Floor plan and premises zoning certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality refuses the licence because the premises is non-conforming, apply for a minor variance or restrictive covenant removal; if the fire inspection identifies deficiencies, remediate and request reinspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Municipal Affairs – Safety Services (Building and Fire) and local municipal Community Development/Business Licence Department
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal General Business Licence and Occupancy Permit for Mail-Order Retail / Distribution Warehouse

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) – Environmental Assessment Program
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA. A low-impact mail-order retail warehouse is below the mandatory assessment thresholds of the Environmental Assessment (Mandatory and Exempt) Regulation, AR 111/1993; a site-specific registration/screening would only apply if the facility handles hazardous materials, large dry storage, or other listed activities above the prescribed thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater or stationary VOC emissions are expected. Sanitary sewage must conform to municipal sewer use bylaws; wastewater discharges to water bodies must comply with the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act and Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives for any negligible odour/combustion emissions. Solid waste and packaging are subject to municipal recycling and Alberta waste management rules under the Waste Control Regulation, AR 192/1996; any generated refrigerants must follow the Ozone-depleting Substances and Halocarbon Alternatives Regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance and Certificate of Compliance under the Alberta Fire Code, AR 75/2009; building occupancy permit under the Alberta Building Code based on structural/floor load review; occupational health and safety clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, RSA 2000, c O-2 and the OHS Code 2020, including workplace hazard assessment, first aid requirements, and employer registration with the Workers' Compensation Board (WCB).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; portal: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses/business-account.html); corporate registry: Alberta Corporate Registry (Alberta Registries)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Alberta ULC must first complete incorporation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, then obtain a federal Business Number (BN) via online registration or Form RC1 ('Request for a Business Number'). The registration process establishes program accounts: RC0001 (corporation income tax), RT (GST/HST), RM (import/export), and payroll accounts where applicable. Supporting identification includes certificate of incorporation, Alberta registry extract, principal/director IDs, and non-resident ownership declarations. CRA issues the 9-digit BN and assigns a CRA program identifier immediately upon validation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no domestic check-the-box election; the ULC is statutorily deemed a corporation under the Income Tax Act and files a T2 corporate return. The ULC is pass-through eligible only for foreign tax purposes: a U.S. federal Form 8832 election may treat the ULC as a disregarded entity or partnership, subject to the Canada-U.S. Tax Treaty tie-breaker (Article IV(6)). Canadian hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss. 18.4-18.6) may restrict deductions arising from any asymmetric classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax — Alberta applies only the 5% federal GST; there is no provincial sales tax or HST in Alberta
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies made in Canada (excluding GST/HST), measured over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters or a single calendar quarter; non-residents may voluntarily register below threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control mandate, or digital stamping in force. GST/HST registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding C$1,500,000 must file electronically via GST/HST NETFILE or EDI. Pan-Canadian Peppol e-invoicing is voluntary.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Tangible personal property exported by the ULC in the course of commercial activity is zero-rated under section 23 of the Excise Tax Act. The supplier must ship the goods to a non-resident destination, transfer title and risk outside Canada, and retain evidence of export within a reasonable time (CRA administrative benchmark: within 60 days of sale/shipment). Services supplied to non-residents on a mail-order/COD e-commerce basis may be zero-rated under section 22 where the performed service is delivered for enjoyment outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Export Declaration (B13A) or CERS electronic export transmission where export value equals or exceeds C$2,000, or for controlled/regulated goods
Commercial invoice / sales invoice indicating zero-rated (0% GST/HST) status and mail-order retail terms (ISIC 4791)
Bill of lading / airway waybill / carrier manifest covering the outbound shipment
Proof of export: carrier tracking, port manifest, destination customs entry or import clearance evidence
Foreign-buyer identification and destination evidence (address, contact details, buyer account records)
Cash-on-delivery settlement records: logistics/courier payout statements, local remittance reconciliation reports
Inward remittance certificate or bank/Airwallex FX statement demonstrating repatriation of export proceeds within 180 days
Sales contract / purchase order evidencing passage of title and risk to the non-resident purchaser
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may deny zero-rating and reassess GST at 5% plus interest when export substantiation is incomplete. False or deceptive statements attract penalties under Excise Tax Act ss. 281.1 and 327: gross-negligence penalty of $100 plus 25% of the net tax sought, and criminal liability with fines and/or imprisonment up to five years for wilful evasion. Misrepresentation extends the normal four-year reassessment period to up to ten years and permits retrospective clawback of export refund claims. Canada imposes no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline, but failure to evidence 180-day repatriation raises audit risk of diverted proceeds or fabricated export transactions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) - the central issuing and monetary authority - in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential supervision of Schedule I banks and authorized foreign-exchange dealers; the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/CFT surveillance of cross-border remittances and money services businesses; the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) and Statistics Canada for export declarations and balance-of-payments statistics; and Global Affairs Canada for economic sanctions administration. Canada maintains no dedicated foreign-exchange-control commission; exchange policy under the Bank of Canada Act and the Currency Act is market-based, requiring no license or approval for private FX conversion or cross-border settlement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is a freely floating currency fully convertible on both the current and capital accounts. Canada observes IMF Article VIII obligations and imposes no exchange-control restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distribution, loan repayment, or liquidation proceeds. The operative hurdles are tax and documentary only: (i) Part XIII non-resident withholding tax applies at a statutory rate of 25%, generally treaty-reduced to 5% to 15% on dividends and 0% to 10% on arm's-length interest under the 1980 Canada-United States Tax Convention (as amended by the 2023 Protocol); (ii) an Alberta ULC owned by a US person can elect flow-through treatment under subsection 216.3(1) of the Income Tax Act so that the US shareholder bears the Canadian tax on the ULC's income; CRA form T2054 and a Canadian tax memorandum must be in place before any distribution; (iii) combined federal (15%) and Alberta (8%) corporate income tax reaches approximately 23% on Alberta-allocated taxable income, and the ULC will not qualify for the federal small business deduction when its controlling shareholder is a US resident. The only material convertibility constraint in this scope is source-country: emerging-market cash-on-delivery collections denominated in restricted currencies must first be exchanged by a locally licensed money changer into USD or EUR through a regional clearing hub before the balance can be wired to Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion timeline, or conversion ratio for export proceeds. The exporter may hold foreign currency balances indefinitely in any Canadian Schedule I bank account or FINTRAC-registered multi-currency wallet. Obligations that do apply: (i) a CBSA B13A Export Declaration must be filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System for each shipment exceeding CAD 2,000, matched to invoice and airway-bill data; (ii) Statistics Canada's Canadian International Merchandise Trade and Balance of Payments surveys require periodic reporting of export values, currencies, and financial flows; (iii) FINTRAC cross-border currency reports are due on physical cash or monetary instruments crossing the border in either direction above CAD 10,000, including cash carried by third-party logistics agents in COD corridors; and (iv) for a ULC with a US shareholder, the controlled foreign affiliate rules (sections 91 to 95 of the Income Tax Act) may attribute income of any foreign incorporated collection entity, and Part XIII deems dividends on certain shareholder-level loans. There is zero forced conversion ratio; banks report FX conversions for statistical purposes only.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (AB ULC under ABCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or extra-provincial registration; recurring annual obligation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty imposed by Corporate Registry; continued default may lead to notice and administrative strike-off or dissolution under the Alberta Business Corporations Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within six months after the end of the taxation year; instalment payments may be required before year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under Income Tax Act s.162: 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; interest accrues on unpaid amounts; repeated default may trigger prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Return (annual or periodic, depending on assigned reporting period)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers must file and remit within three months after fiscal year-end; monthly or quarterly filers follow the assigned reporting period deadlines.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties and interest under the Excise Tax Act apply to late, missing, or incorrect filings; continued non-compliance may result in assessments and collection actions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general revenue- or asset-based audit threshold for a non-offering Alberta ULC; independent audit is mandatory for offering corporations and may be waived by unanimous shareholder consent for private corporations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) election for private enterprises; financial statements must be approved by directors and made available to shareholders.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: ABCA requires the ULC to maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control and to take reasonable steps at least once each fiscal year to confirm and update all significant control holders, including identity, residency, shareholding percentage, and acquisition event. This register is not filed with Alberta Corporate Registry but must be produced on demand to the Registrar or law enforcement authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (UBO Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - USD 1,500 per annum depending on service provider and corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 18,000 per annum depending on transaction volume, payment rail complexity, and register maintenance procedures

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (federal 9% on first $500,000 active business income if CCPC; Alberta 2% on first $500,000), SR&ED investment tax credits (35% refundable for CCPCs, 15% non-refundable for others), Alberta Innovation Employment Grant, and accelerated capital cost allowance for certain clean energy equipment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal) and AT1 (Alberta Corporate Tax Return) combined via the T2 form; filed electronically through CRA's e-file or NETFILE (mandatory for most corporations).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end (e.g., for a December 31 year-end, due June 30). Instalments are due quarterly if net tax owing exceeds $3,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue (gross receipts from mail-order retail sales, including COD amounts).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Canadian-source revenue; if non-resident, allocate based on permanent establishment in Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses (cost of goods sold, logistics, payment processing fees, COD remittance costs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses reasonably incurred to earn Canadian-source income are deductible; transfer pricing adjustments may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (after applying loss carryovers and deductions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must compute taxable income attributable to Canadian business carried on through a permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal and provincial tax payable before credits (combined rate 23%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty provisions if applicable; otherwise, full 23% applies to Canadian-source business income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (e.g., foreign tax credits, investment tax credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim only credits directly related to Canadian-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax payable (after credits and instalments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure instalments paid; late payment interest applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month (up to 12 months). Repeated failure: 10% penalty. Daily interest on unpaid amounts at prescribed rate (currently 8% for corporations). Failure to file electronically may incur a $250 penalty.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on dividends paid to non-residents (subject to treaty reduction).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding under a tax treaty, the non-resident recipient must provide a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) from their home tax authority to the Canadian payer before payment. The payer then applies the treaty rate (e.g., 5% for US corporate shareholders holding ≥10% voting shares, 15% otherwise). Form NR301 is used to certify treaty entitlement. Retroactive refunds are possible via Form T7B (for dividends) within two years of payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25% (treaty rate often 10% or 0% for certain IP). Interest: statutory 25% but exempt for arm's length non-resident lenders (subject to conditions); treaty rates typically 10% or 0%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File required if gross revenue exceeds CAD 50 million, or assets exceed CAD 10 million, or transactions with non-resident related parties exceed CAD 1 million (for services) or CAD 5 million (for goods). For this e-commerce entity, if cross-border related-party transactions (e.g., logistics or payment processing) exceed CAD 1 million, documentation is mandatory.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have a separate ESR regime, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and the 'permanent establishment' concept require real economic substance. A ULC must demonstrate actual business operations, employees, and decision-making in Alberta to avoid recharacterization. The CRA may apply the 'substance over form' doctrine to deny treaty benefits if the entity is a shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of COD revenue, false deductions, or failure to file T2 returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act (s. 239): fines up to 200% of tax evaded, imprisonment up to 5 years. Civil penalties: 50% gross negligence penalty on understated tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax withholdings (e.g., payroll, GST) under s. 227.1. For tax evasion, directors may face personal fines and imprisonment if they directed or acquiesced.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: ULC has no physical office, no employees, and no substantive business activity in Alberta; used solely to route profits to non-residents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA can deny treaty benefits, reallocate income under s. 247 (transfer pricing), and apply GAAR to disregard the entity. Penalties: 10% of the adjustment amount for transfer pricing mispricing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed for the corporation's tax liabilities if the CRA pierces the corporate veil due to fraud or sham. Travel bans under the Income Tax Act (s. 238) for non-payment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Cash on Delivery (COD) Money Laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML compliance for COD transactions, accepting large cash payments without reporting, or structuring transactions to avoid reporting thresholds (CAD 10,000).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA): fines up to CAD 2 million for corporations, criminal charges for directors/officers. FINTRAC administrative penalties up to CAD 1 million per violation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined up to CAD 500,000 and imprisoned up to 5 years for knowingly failing to report or for laundering proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain contemporaneous TP documentation, or pricing intercompany transactions (e.g., logistics fees, payment processing) not at arm's length.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may adjust taxable income and apply penalties of 10% of the net adjustment (if documentation incomplete). Interest on reassessments applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they signed false or misleading documents. In severe cases, criminal prosecution for tax evasion.
